2609.09324.title: Improving 5G AI-RAN MCS Selection by Predicting Retransmissions
2609.09324.paper_summary: Link Adaptation (LA) in 5G NR is inherently reactive, relying on channel measurements and HARQ feedback that may become quickly obsolete when the channel changes quickly. This data is also noisy, making it hard to track accurately, and has to be fed to real-time controllers with feedback-loop effects which are hard to troubleshoot. This explains why most practical deployments select simple but robust algorithms, which accept that the lag can leave the scheduler operating at overly aggressive or unnecessarily conservative rates, trading spectrum efficiency for predictable performance. In this paper, we improve on this status-quo with NOSTRAdAMUS, a predictive LA framework which adds foresight to existing algorithms without replacing or redesigning them. NOSTRAdAMUS predicts whether a retransmission will occur in the next radio frame from recent HARQ history, and applies corrections to the Modulation and Coding Scheme (MCS) selected by the underlying policy. We benchmark several ML models and show that Gradient Boosting achieves 82.9% accuracy overall with high-confidence interventions that are correct 94.2% of the time, and an inference latency of 5.5 μs. We train the model based on data collected Over-the-Air (OTA) on the X5G testbed, using the open-source OpenAirInterface (OAI) 5G stack, NVIDIA Aerial, and COTS O-RAN Radio Units and User Equipments. The model is then deployed as a dApp, which we evaluate OTA as well as on various channels with hardware-in-the-loop channel emulators. This includes 3GPP TDL and CDL channels, SISO and MIMO configurations, and pedestrian and vehicular mobility. Our evaluation shows that without retraining, and across this variety of scenarios, the dApp augments two SOTA LA algorithms, and increases goodput by up to 71.5% while reducing retransmissions by up to 71.8%. This demonstrates the robustness and generalization capabilities of our approach.
2609.09324.paper_summary_zh: 在5G NR中，鏈路適應（LA）本質上是反應性的，依賴於通道測量和HARQ反饋，而這些在通道快速變化時可能迅速過時。這些數據也很嘈雜，難以準確追蹤，並且必須提供給具有反饋循環效應的實時控制器，這些效應難以排除故障。這解釋了為什麼大多數實際部署選擇簡單但穩健的算法，這些算法接受延遲可能使調度器以過於激進或不必要保守的速率運行，將頻譜效率與可預測性能進行權衡。在本文中，我們通過NOSTRAdAMUS改進了這一現狀，這是一個預測性LA框架，為現有算法增加了前瞻性，而不需要替換或重新設計它們。NOSTRAdAMUS根據最近的HARQ歷史預測下一個無線幀中是否會發生重傳，並對底層策略所選擇的調製和編碼方案（MCS）進行修正。我們基準測試了幾個機器學習模型，顯示梯度提升總體準確率達到82.9%，並且高置信度的干預正確率達到94.2%，推斷延遲為5.5微秒。我們基於在X5G測試平台上收集的空中（OTA）數據訓練模型，使用開源的OpenAirInterface（OAI）5G堆棧、NVIDIA Aerial以及商用O-RAN無線單元和用戶設備。然後將模型作為dApp部署，我們在OTA以及使用硬件在環路的通道模擬器的各種通道上進行評估。這包括3GPP TDL和CDL通道、SISO和MIMO配置，以及行人和車輛移動。我們的評估顯示，在不重新訓練的情況下，並且在這種多樣的場景中，dApp增強了兩個最先進的LA算法，並將有效吞吐量提高了最多71.5%，同時將重傳減少了最多71.8%。這展示了我們方法的穩健性和泛化能力。
